encounters.cc: Intermittent numbness and tingling in left arm and leg, and episodes of blurred vision in right eye that resolve spontaneously.

lines: Intermittent numbness and tingling in left arm and leg, and episodes of blurred vision in right eye that resolve spontaneously.
A 32-year-old Caucasian woman presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of intermittent numbness and tingling in her left arm and leg.
She also reports episodes of blurred vision in her right eye that seem to resolve spontaneously.
- Interferon beta-1a 44 mcg subcutaneous injection three times weekly
- Oxybutynin 5 mg oral twice daily as needed for urinary urgency
- No known first-degree relatives with multiple sclerosis
She does not smoke. She moved to the northern United States from the south two years ago.
Afferent pupillary defect in the right eye and hyperreflexia in the left upper and lower extremities
MRI of the brain with and without contrast shows multiple periventricular white matter lesions

encounters.cc: Blurred vision in left eye and electric shock sensation radiating down spine when bending neck forward.

lines: Blurred vision in left eye and electric shock sensation radiating down spine when bending neck forward.

The patient with RRMS and optic neuritis returns to clinic one year after initial presentation with left-sided numbness and right eye blurred vision and presents to clinic with a 2-day history of blurred vision in her left eye and a sensation of electric shock radiating down her spine when she bends her neck forward.
She also reports intermittent numbness and tingling in her right hand over the past month.
- Interferon beta-1a 44 mcg subcutaneous injection three times weekly
- Oxybutynin 5 mg oral twice daily as needed for urinary urgency
- No known first-degree relatives with multiple sclerosis
On examination, her left eye has an afferent pupillary defect, and there is decreased sensation to light touch in her right hand.
Visual acuity is reduced in the left eye.
The remainder of the neurologic examination is normal.
The patient's most recent laboratory results are as follows:
Brain MRI with and without contrast is performed and reveals multiple periventricular white matter lesions, some of which enhance with gadolinium.

encounters.cc: Several weeks of worsening right eye pain and blurry vision with color desaturation.

lines: Several weeks of worsening right eye pain and blurry vision with color desaturation.
The patient returns for evaluation of recurrent visual symptoms following prior bilateral optic neuritis and previous blurred vision episodes in both eyes.
She reports pain that worsens with eye movement and some color desaturation.
- Interferon beta-1a 44 mcg subcutaneous injection three times weekly
- Oxybutynin 5 mg oral twice daily as needed for urinary urgency
- No known first-degree relatives with multiple sclerosis
Neurologic exam reveals decreased visual acuity and a relative afferent pupillary defect in the right eye.
MRI of the brain shows multiple periventricular white matter lesions oriented perpendicularly to the ventricles, along with T2 hyperintensities in the corpus callosum.
Biopsy of a lesion would show infiltration by lymphocytes and macrophages with reactive astrocytes.

orders.indication: R eye pain with vision loss

encounters.cc: Episodes of sudden urinary leakage and urgency that have become more noticeable, causing hesitation to leave home.

lines: Episodes of sudden urinary leakage and urgency that have become more noticeable, causing hesitation to leave home.
The patient returns for evaluation of worsening urinary symptoms in the context of neurogenic bladder and relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis previously managed by Neurology.
She describes an unpredictable loss of urine that tends to occur suddenly and without much warning, sometimes even before she can reach the bathroom.
She also notes an uncomfortable sensation that builds quickly and compels her to void immediately.
These symptoms have made her hesitant to leave home for extended periods.
Her past medical history includes several episodes over the past year of visual disturbance and weakness affecting different limbs at different times, each resolving over days.
She was evaluated by a neurologist and underwent imaging that showed scattered lesions in the brain and spinal cord.
- Interferon beta-1a 44 mcg subcutaneous injection three times weekly
- Oxybutynin 5 mg oral twice daily as needed for urinary urgency
- No known first-degree relatives with multiple sclerosis
On examination, she has increased tone in the lower extremities, brisk reflexes, and reduced proprioception in the feet.
No abdominal or pelvic masses are noted.

encounters.cc: Fever, chills, and dysuria with increased urinary frequency over the past week.

lines: Fever, chills, and dysuria with increased urinary frequency over the past week.

The patient is a 32-year-old woman with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis since age 27 and neurogenic bladder with detrusor overactivity who returns for evaluation following her urology visit three months prior.
She presents to the outpatient clinic with a 2-day history of fever, chills, and dysuria.
She reports that she has been experiencing increased urinary frequency and urgency for the past week.
She has a known neurogenic bladder due to her multiple sclerosis and has been managing her urinary symptoms with clean intermittent catheterization for the past year.
Her last urinary tract infection was three months ago.
- Interferon beta-1a 44 mcg subcutaneous injection three times weekly
- Oxybutynin 5 mg oral twice daily as needed for urinary urgency
- No known first-degree relatives with multiple sclerosis
Temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, and heart rate is 88 beats per minute
On physical examination, her abdomen is soft and non-tender.
There is no costovertebral angle tenderness.

encounters.cc: Intermittent visual blurring in right eye, involuntary muscle spasms of left hand, and urinary urgency with frequency.

lines: Intermittent visual blurring in right eye, involuntary muscle spasms of left hand, and urinary urgency with frequency.
The patient with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis, recurrent optic neuritis, and neurogenic bladder returns with new visual and urinary symptoms similar to prior relapses.
These started 10 days ago with sudden, sharp pain behind her right eye followed by difficulty focusing, especially in low light.
She also notes frequent, urgent restroom trips, totaling over 10 urinations daily, with occasional loss of urinary control.
- Interferon beta-1a 44 mcg subcutaneous injection three times weekly
- Oxybutynin 5 mg oral twice daily as needed for urinary urgency
Family history is negative for neurodegenerative disorders, but her mother has systemic lupus erythematosus.
Neurologic examination demonstrates hyperreflexia and clonus in the left upper extremity, along with decreased sensation to vibration in the right lower limb.
Cranial nerve assessment reveals a subtle afferent pupillary defect on the right.
Funduscopic exam is notable for mild optic disc swelling.
MRI of the brain shows multiple hyperintense lesions in the periventricular white matter.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset right leg weakness and numbness, with blurred vision in left eye that started one week ago.

lines: Sudden onset right leg weakness and numbness, with blurred vision in left eye that started one week ago.

This 33-year-old female with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis and recurrent bilateral optic neuritis returns to the emergency department with a 2-day history of sudden onset right leg weakness and numbness.
She also reports blurred vision in her left eye that started a week ago.
Her past medical history is significant for multiple sclerosis (MS), diagnosed 5 years ago, with two previous episodes of optic neuritis and one episode of sensory symptoms.
She has been on interferon beta-1a since her diagnosis.
She does not take any other medications.
- Oxybutynin 5 mg oral twice daily as needed for urinary urgency
She has no known drug allergies
- No known first-degree relatives with multiple sclerosis
On examination, her right lower extremity shows a strength of 3/5, increased tone, and hyperreflexia.
Visual acuity is decreased in the left eye, with an afferent pupillary defect.
MRI of the brain with gadolinium shows multiple periventricular white matter lesions, with one enhancing lesion.

encounters.cc: Progressive weakness in both legs with difficulty walking, numbness below navel, and urinary retention since morning.

lines: Progressive weakness in both legs with difficulty walking, numbness below navel, and urinary retention since morning.
The patient with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder returns for evaluation following prior unilateral weakness.
She reports difficulty walking with several falls at home, numbness below her navel, and has been unable to void since morning.
Her past medical history is significant for an episode of blurred vision in her right eye two years ago, which resolved spontaneously.
- Interferon beta-1a 44 mcg subcutaneous injection three times weekly
- Oxybutynin 5 mg oral twice daily as needed for urinary urgency
- No known first-degree relatives with multiple sclerosis
On examination, her strength is 2/5 in both lower extremities, and she has decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick below the T6 dermatome.
Deep tendon reflexes are brisk in the lower extremities, and Babinski sign is positive bilaterally.
MRI of the spinal cord reveals a hyperintense lesion on T2-weighted images at the T4 level.
